h1: The 7 Best 18-Inch Lawn Mowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven 18-inch lawn mowers across gas, cordless and manual reel, compared on engine, drive, deck and the yard each suits.
summary: The Wild Badger 40V is the best 18-inch lawn mower, a quiet brushless cordless model with no gas to handle. The PowerSmart EasyCut 144cc is the top gas pick, and its steel-deck sibling handles rough ground. The Great States and LawnMaster are push reels for small, tidy lawns.
intro: An 18-inch deck is the sweet spot for small and mid-size yards: wide enough to avoid endless passes, narrow enough to slip through a side gate. But 18 inches comes in three completely different machines, gas, cordless and manual reel, and the right one depends far more on your upkeep tolerance than on the deck. The cut width is the same, but the weekly chores are not.

We reviewed seven 18-inch mowers on paper, ranking them on power source, deck material, height adjustment and the yard type each suits. We relied on the spec lines and owner feedback, with no lab-style claims. Prices cluster between $50 and $200, so the useful comparison is what you will be doing in the garage afterward: charging, fueling or sharpening.

products.name: Wild Badger Power 40V 18-Inch Brushless Cordless Electric Lawn Mower
products.verdict: A quiet brushless cordless mower with no gas to handle.
products.description:
The Wild Badger has an 18-inch deck, a 40V brushless motor and a cordless battery platform, in the $100 to $200 bracket. A brushless motor has no carbon brushes to wear out, which makes it more efficient and longer lived than a brushed one. Pair that with a battery and you lose gas, oil and the pull cord.

It ranks first because it removes the chores that put people off mowing while keeping the full 18-inch width. Against the gas PowerSmart models below, you give up unlimited runtime but gain quiet, low-maintenance operation. The self-propelled 40V model has drive but a thinner record.

Buy it for a small yard where quiet matters. The caveat is runtime: it depends on the battery you get, and a second pack costs extra over time.
products.idealFor: Small yards where quiet, low-maintenance mowing matters.
products.skipIf: You want unlimited runtime from a gas tank.

products.name: PowerSmart EasyCut 18-Inch Gas Lawn Mower, 144cc 4-Cycle Engine
products.verdict: A light 144cc 4-cycle gas mower with 5 height positions.
products.description:
The PowerSmart EasyCut has an 18-inch deck, a 144cc four-cycle gas engine, side discharge and five-position height adjustment, in the $100 to $200 bracket. A four-cycle engine runs on plain gasoline with a separate oil sump, so there is no fuel mixing, and 144cc is plenty for an 18-inch deck.

It ranks second because it is the best of the gas mowers for ordinary yards. It beats the Wild Badger on runtime flexibility, with no battery to run flat halfway across the lawn, and it undercuts nothing on price. Five height positions cover most seasonal cuts. It also runs lighter than its steel-deck sibling.

Choose it for a modest yard that suits a light gas mower. The caveat is gas and oil upkeep, plus noise that the cordless pick avoids.

products.name: PowerSmart EasyCut 18-Inch Gas Lawn Mower, 144cc OHV Engine, Steel Deck
products.verdict: A steel-deck gas mower for roots, curbs and rougher terrain.
products.description:
This PowerSmart has an 18-inch steel deck, a 144cc OHV engine and five-position dual-lever height adjustment, in the $100 to $200 bracket. A steel deck resists dents and cracks where plastic can split, and dual levers let you adjust the front and rear wheels together or separately.

It ranks third because the steel deck is its edge over the otherwise similar four-cycle model, standing up better to roots and curbs. It sits in the same bracket, so you pay no premium for the toughness. The OHV engine design is common and well understood, which keeps parts easy to find. Against the cordless picks, it is louder and heavier.

Choose it for yards with roots, curbs or uneven ground. The caveat is that steel adds weight, which you feel on slopes and when turning at the end of a row.
products.idealFor: Yards with roots, curbs or rough terrain.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is flat and smooth.

products.name: 18-Inch 40V Max Brushless Cordless Self-Propelled Lawn Mower
products.verdict: The only 18 inch cordless here with self-propelled drive.
products.description:
This 40V Max mower has an 18-inch deck, a brushless motor and self-propelled drive on a cordless platform, in the $100 to $200 bracket. Self-propelled drive turns the wheels for you, so pushing a loaded mower up a slope takes less effort, and it is a rare feature in a cordless 18-inch.

It ranks fourth because it comes from a newer, unproven seller, even though self-propel is a real advantage on slopes. The Wild Badger sits in the same bracket with a more complete platform and no drive. Drive systems add weight and moving parts, which is a risk with a thin track record.

Choose it if you want drive assistance on a cordless 18-inch deck. The caveat is the unproven brand: warranty and battery replacement may be harder to get, so check the seller's terms.
products.idealFor: Cordless buyers who want drive assistance.

products.name: Great States 815-18 18-Inch 5-Blade Push Reel Lawn Mower
products.verdict: A quiet five-blade reel with no gas, battery or cord.
products.description:
The Great States 815-18 is an 18-inch push reel mower with five blades and no gas, battery or cord, in the $100 to $200 bracket. A reel cuts like scissors, with the blades turning against a fixed bed knife, which gives a cleaner cut than a rotary blade when the grass is short and the lawn is flat.

It ranks fifth because manual power suits only certain lawns. It costs more than the LawnMaster reel below, and neither handles tall grass well, so you must mow before the lawn gets away. The five-blade reel is quiet and requires no fuel or charging. Against the cordless picks, you lose the ability to cut thick grass.

Choose it for a flat, tidy lawn of small size. The caveat is that tall grass is hard to push through, and any miss means you cut twice.
products.skipIf: You let the grass grow long.

products.name: LawnMaster LMRM1801 Push Reel Lawn Mower 18-Inch 5-Blade
products.verdict: A five-blade manual reel for less than $100.
products.description:
The LawnMaster LMRM1801 is an 18-inch push reel with five blades and no gas, battery or cord, in the $50 to $100 bracket. Like all reels, it has no engine, so storage is easy and noise is nearly nonexistent.

It ranks sixth because it matches the Great States on design but costs less, in the $50 to $100 bracket, which makes it the entry point. The ranking gap is small. The two share the same five-blade layout and the same limits on tall grass and rough ground. The price difference is a full bracket.

Choose it on a budget for a small, regularly maintained lawn. The caveat is that, like any reel, it needs frequent mowing, and a weekly schedule is the practical minimum.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers with small, tidy lawns.
products.skipIf: Your grass gets long between cuts.

products.name: PowerSmart 18-Inch 144cc Gas Lawn Mower, Push Mower with Side-Discharge
products.verdict: A no-frills 144cc gas push mower with side discharge.
products.description:
This PowerSmart is an 18-inch push mower with a 144cc gas engine and side discharge, in the $100 to $200 bracket. Side discharge throws clippings out of the deck, which is the simplest and cheapest design to build and maintain.

It ranks last because it lists fewer details than the EasyCut models, such as height positions or deck material, so you cannot tell how it differs from them. It does the basic job at the same price tier. With no bagging option, you either mulch or leave clippings in a windrow.

Choose it for a simple gas push mower without a bagging kit. The caveat is that missing bag option, and the thin listing means you should confirm height adjustment before ordering.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a basic gas push mower.

whatMatters.detail: Gas gives long runtime but needs fuel and oil. Cordless is quiet but limited by the battery. A reel needs no power but your effort. Check the title for gas, cordless or reel, and think about where you will store fuel or charge batteries. The power source sets your weekly chores more than the deck size does, so decide it first.

A steel deck resists dents from roots and curbs better than lighter plastic. It adds weight. Look for the material in the listing bullets. The steel-deck PowerSmart states it, and the other decks do not say. If your yard has stumps, rocks or curbs, durability matters more than weight savings, and a steel deck repays the extra pounds.

More positions let you tune cut height for the season, higher in summer heat and lower in spring. Five positions is common, as on the PowerSmart EasyCut. Check the stated number, and whether levers adjust all wheels at once. Reels adjust differently from rotary mowers, so read the manual before you set the height.

A 144cc four-cycle or OHV engine runs on straight gas with separate oil, so there is no mixing. It is simpler than a two-stroke. Check the engine line on the listing, and confirm whether the oil is changed or topped up. A brushless motor on the cordless mowers plays the same simplicity role, and needs no engine oil at all.

Side discharge throws clippings out the side, and bagging catches them. Some models have no bag option, like the simplest PowerSmart. Check what the listing says about mulching and bagging, because bagging matters for leaves and for lawns with weeds that you do not want to spread, while mulching suits frequent cuts.

faq.a: It suits small to mid-size yards. Larger lawns need more passes and more time, so consider a wider deck. For a quarter acre or less, 18 inches is comfortable, and it fits through narrow gates.
They pick by deck width and ignore power source. Gas, cordless and reel need very different upkeep, so choose the one you will actually maintain, then compare decks, engines and prices.

faq.q: Is cordless worth it over gas?
faq.a: For small yards, yes. For long sessions, a gas PowerSmart has no battery to run flat. The Wild Badger is quieter and lower maintenance, but a second battery adds cost and a charger needs a spot in the garage.

faq.q: How do I start a gas mower?
faq.a: Add fuel and oil per the manual and pull the cord. Follow all safety steps, wear closed shoes, check the oil level first and keep hands clear of the blade. Prime if the manual says so, and let the engine warm for a minute before you start mowing.

faq.q: How do I maintain a reel mower?
faq.a: Keep the blades clean and adjusted. Consult the manual for blade contact guidance, because a reel cuts well only when the blades just touch the bed knife.

faq.q: Can I use a reel on rough ground?
faq.a: It is a poor fit. A reel stops on roots and bumps, so the steel-deck PowerSmart handles roots and curbs better. Reels like the Great States suit flat, tidy lawns, not uneven ground.

finalTake: Buy the Wild Badger for a small yard where noise and upkeep matter. Choose a PowerSmart gas mower if runtime is the worry, the steel-deck version for roots and curbs, and a reel only if you mow often. Match the power source to your tolerance for maintenance before looking at anything else.
